hero.headline: Asian markets plunge as tech stocks sell off and oil prices surge on Middle East strikes
hero.body:
Asian stock markets fell sharply as technology stocks continued a global selloff and oil prices jumped following Iranian missile strikes on Israel. South Korea's Kospi index plunged more than 5%, while markets in Japan also declined after weeks of gains in tech-related shares. U.S. stock futures traded mixed as investors assessed the escalating tensions in the Middle East.

The technology sector bore the brunt of selling pressure across the region. South Korean tech heavyweights followed a significant decline in Wall Street's artificial intelligence-linked stocks. On Thursday, the U.S. benchmark S&P 500 and Dow Jones industrial average each closed down 1.7%, while the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.3%. Major tech companies like Nvidia, valued at $4.5 trillion, led stocks lower, declining 3.6% as it continues to face fallout from Japanese investor SoftBank's disclosure that it had sold its entire stake in the firm for $5.8 billion.

The selloff reflects broader concerns that technology firms may now be overvalued after an extraordinary rally driven by artificial intelligence optimism that had propelled global stock markets to record highs. Analysts described the current situation as a correction in the artificial intelligence sector combined with market rotation. "There's a lot of uncertainties about the state of the economy," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities. "What we're going through is a little bit of a correction in the market in the AI sector and we're seeing market rotation."

Oil prices climbed more than three dollars per barrel after Iran fired missiles at Israel, raising doubts about the fragile ceasefire in the region. The attacks put renewed pressure on energy markets already strained by the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz, which has stranded vast amounts of the world's oil supply. The price surge came even as OPEC Plus announced plans to increase output by 188,000 barrels per day, a move analysts described as largely symbolic given current supply constraints.

The dual pressures of geopolitical risk and sector-specific weakness created difficult conditions across Asia-Pacific markets. Investors shifted focus from growth stocks to assessing the potential economic impact of prolonged Middle East conflict. The combination of rising energy costs and falling equity values raised concerns about broader market stability.

The developments marked a sharp reversal from recent optimism. Market confidence has also been tested by remarks from senior Federal Reserve officials on interest rate policy, as well as uncertainty surrounding the U.S. economy following a lengthy government shutdown. Analysts pointed to how quickly market sentiment can shift when geopolitical events intersect with sector-specific weakness, underscoring the interconnection between energy security and technology sector performance.

cards.headline: Trump urges Netanyahu not to retaliate against Iran missile attack
cards.teaser: President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu not to retaliate against Iran's missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy, according to.
cards.body:
President Trump called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, urging him to refrain from retaliating against Iran's missile attack and to pursue diplomatic solutions instead. Trump had previously indicated his intention to make this appeal to Netanyahu.

Despite Trump's request, the Israeli Air Force struck Iranian military targets in central and western Iran on Monday morning. The strikes marked Israel's first direct attack on Iran since an April ceasefire and were launched in response to Iran's initial missile barrage. Trump has rejected suggestions that the escalating conflict contradicts his 2024 campaign pledge to avoid new wars.

cards.headline: Airlines face $100 billion fuel cost increase as Middle East conflict disrupts oil supply
cards.teaser: Global airlines slashed profit forecasts as jet fuel costs surge due to war-related supply disruptions.
cards.body:
Airlines are grappling with a $100 billion surge in jet fuel costs this year due to Middle East disruptions driving up energy prices. The International Air Transport Association warned that the crisis has cut expected airline profitability for 2026 in half, prompting carriers to revise their financial forecasts downward.

Airlines say fare increases are inevitable as they work to offset the mounting operating expenses. The spike in fuel costs reflects broader market turmoil, with oil production constrained by effective closures of critical shipping routes and geopolitical tensions limiting global supply.

cards.headline: Strong Earthquake Hits Philippines, Prompts Tsunami Warnings Across Asia
cards.teaser: A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the southern Philippines, toppling buildings and triggering regional tsunami alerts.
cards.body:
A 7.8 magnitude earthquake centered at sea struck southern Philippines early Monday, causing buildings to collapse and killing at least three people. The powerful quake knocked out power in affected areas and triggered immediate rescue operations, with authorities working to assess the full extent of damage across multiple locations.

The earthquake sparked tsunami warnings across the region, with officials warning of waves up to three metres in parts of the Philippines and smaller waves possible in Indonesia and Malaysia. Hawaii officials reported no tsunami threat to the islands.

cards.headline: Extreme Heat Pushes Pakistani District to 125 Degrees
cards.teaser: Residents of Dadu District in Pakistan endured temperatures reaching 125 degrees as climate extremes intensify.
cards.body:
Dadu District in Pakistan faced temperatures reaching 125 degrees as residents searched for shade during extreme heat. The area is prone to multiple climate challenges including sandstorms, drought, and flooding. Each season brings different struggles for people living in the district.

The extreme temperatures represent the latest in a series of climate-related hardships for the region. Residents must contend with shifting weather patterns that bring both intense heat and severe flooding at different times of year. The district's vulnerability to climate extremes continues to affect daily life and livelihoods.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft unveil AI-focused chips and computers at Computex
cards.body:
Nvidia and Microsoft announced new computer hardware designed for artificial intelligence at the Computex trade show in Taiwan, marking a significant shift in how the tech industry approaches personal computing.

Nvidia introduced the RTX Spark, a superchip that integrates both a microprocessor and graphics processing capabilities. The company developed the chip with help from Taiwan's MediaTek and describes it as purpose-built to run AI agents directly on laptops and desktop computers. Rather than relying on cloud-based processing, the RTX Spark enables AI applications to operate locally on devices while maintaining thin, lightweight designs.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced that major computer manufacturers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus and HP will use the RTX Spark chip paired with Microsoft's Windows software. Huang stated the chip would "reinvent the PC" for the AI era, following three years of collaboration between the two companies. He emphasized that the technology could fundamentally change how people interact with computers, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard interfaces with AI agents that navigate PCs autonomously.

The announcement represents Nvidia's expansion beyond its dominant position in data center processors into the consumer PC market. The company is also developing the Vera CPU, designed for AI agents and already being tested by companies including OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX. These moves demonstrate Nvidia's strategy to establish itself across multiple levels of the AI technology stack.

Microsoft showcased the Surface Laptop Ultra, a new device specifically designed to handle AI workloads locally. The laptop incorporates Nvidia's chip technology and represents the companies' shared vision of AI-capable personal computers becoming mainstream consumer products.

Industry analysts view the RTX Spark announcement as historically significant. Neil Shah, a co-founder of Counterpoint Research, compared the moment to the introduction of the iPhone and the emergence of ChatGPT, suggesting the chip could transform PCs from application-focused devices into "agentic AI personal computers." However, analysts also note that establishing a consumer PC business will take considerable time despite Nvidia's current dominance in AI semiconductors.

The announcements signal broader industry competition intensifying in consumer AI chips. Intel announced plans to release an AI chip later this year using cheaper memory and cooling technology, positioning itself against Nvidia and AMD. Intel also unveiled a new graphics processing unit called Xe3P, developed specifically for the emerging generation of AI agents.

During the conference, Huang addressed concerns about AI's impact on employment, stating that suggestions the technology would reduce job demand were "complete nonsense." He argued that AI would increase productivity and lead to greater hiring of software engineers rather than job losses across the industry.

cards.headline: Millions may have unclaimed retirement savings from automatic enrollment
cards.teaser: Workplace pension programs have created accounts some employees may not know exist.
cards.body:
Workers in countries with automatic retirement enrollment may be saving for retirement without realizing it, according to financial advisors. One simple check could ensure individuals are not missing out on employer contributions and investment growth that could help in later life.

Automatic enrollment programs deduct retirement contributions directly from paychecks and often include employer matching funds. Financial experts recommend that workers verify whether they have retirement accounts established through current or former employers, as unclaimed accounts can accumulate significant value over time through both contributions and investment returns.

hero.headline: Strong Earthquake Hits Philippines, Prompts Tsunami Warnings Across Asia
hero.teaser: A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the southern Philippines, toppling buildings and triggering regional tsunami alerts.
hero.body:
A 7.8 magnitude earthquake centered at sea struck southern Philippines early Monday, causing buildings to collapse and killing at least three people. The powerful quake knocked out power in affected areas and triggered immediate rescue operations, with authorities working to assess the full extent of damage across multiple locations.

The earthquake sparked tsunami warnings across the region, with officials warning of waves up to three metres in parts of the Philippines and smaller waves possible in Indonesia and Malaysia. Hawaii officials reported no tsunami threat to the islands.

cards.headline: Peru Presidential Runoff Remains Too Close to Call
cards.teaser: Voting in Peru's presidential runoff ended with the race in a dead heat between a leftist and right-wing candidate.
cards.body:
Peru's presidential runoff pitted two starkly different visions for the country. Keiko Fujimori, a right-wing perennial candidate and daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, faced off against Roberto Sánchez, a leftist congressman and former trade and tourism minister. The race reflected a polarized left-right divide similar to Peru's 2021 election.

Voters confronted a nation struggling with instability and crime. Peru had cycled through eight presidents in a decade, leaving many citizens frustrated and seeking stability. Both candidates offered contrasting approaches: Fujimori campaigned on a tough-on-crime platform, while Sánchez appealed to those seeking broader change. The election would determine who would lead the country as its ninth president in ten years.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth Faces Backlash for D-Day Speech on Immigration
cards.teaser: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth drew criticism for comparing immigration to an invasion during a speech at D-Day commemorations in France.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth drew criticism for remarks made during a D-Day commemoration speech in France, where he characterized European migration policies as an invasion. Observers condemned the comments as inappropriate for the solemn occasion marking the World War II landings.

Residents of the French village hosting the visit said Hegseth was unwelcome following his speech. A House Republican also criticized the remarks as unsuitable for the setting, while commentators described his statements as reflecting "grotesque stupidity."

cards.headline: Asian Tech Stocks Drop After Middle East Missile Strikes
cards.teaser: Markets in South Korea and Japan fell sharply after renewed attacks between Iran and Israel ended a weeks-long tech rally.
cards.body:
Asian technology stocks experienced a sharp decline following escalating Middle East tensions from missile strikes between Iran and Israel. Markets in South Korea and Japan fell after experiencing a strong rally in recent weeks, with South Korea's Kospi index dropping 7 percent as investors reassessed their risk exposure.

The sell-off reflected a broader shift away from riskier assets as geopolitical concerns mounted across global markets. U.S. stock futures showed mixed trading activity as traders worldwide responded to the developing situation.

cards.headline: Extreme Heat Pushes Pakistani District to 125 Degrees
cards.teaser: Residents of Dadu District in Pakistan endured temperatures reaching 125 degrees as climate extremes intensify.
cards.body:
Dadu District in Pakistan faced temperatures reaching 125 degrees as residents searched for shade during extreme heat. The area is prone to multiple climate challenges including sandstorms, drought, and flooding. Each season brings different struggles for people living in the district.

The extreme temperatures represent the latest in a series of climate-related hardships for the region. Residents must contend with shifting weather patterns that bring both intense heat and severe flooding at different times of year. The district's vulnerability to climate extremes continues to affect daily life and livelihoods.

cards.headline: Travel Restrictions Complicate World Cup Access for International Fans
cards.teaser: Fans worldwide say U.S. travel bans and visa regulations make them feel excluded from attending the upcoming World Cup.
cards.body:
International soccer fans worldwide are expressing anger over U.S. travel bans and visa regulations that prevent them from attending the World Cup. Many feel excluded from the tournament, with fans describing it as "a World Cup for them not us." The access barriers have created significant frustration across the global soccer community.

The travel restrictions and visa requirements have sparked broader debate about hosting major international sporting events in countries with restrictive entry policies. The situation highlights tensions between event accessibility and national security measures as the tournament approaches.

cards.headline: Spain Sees Record Tourism as Visitors Avoid Middle East
cards.teaser: Spain recorded its highest-ever visitor numbers for April as tourists redirected travel plans away from the Middle East.
cards.body:
Spain received 9.1 million international visitors in April, marking a record for that month. The surge in tourism reflects a broader shift in travel patterns as visitors seek alternative European destinations amid geopolitical concerns elsewhere.

The strong April figures demonstrate Spain's growing appeal as a preferred travel destination, with the country benefiting from redirected global travel flows away from less stable regions.

hero.headline: Six injured in stabbing attack at Penn Station in Manhattan
hero.body:
Six people were injured in a stabbing attack at Penn Station in Manhattan, with a suspect now in custody, authorities reported. The incident occurred at one of the busiest transportation hubs in the United States, disrupting service and prompting a large police response.

Authorities took a suspect into custody following the attack. The injured victims were transported to area hospitals for treatment. Penn Station serves as a major transit center for commuters traveling through New York City, connecting subway lines, commuter rail, and Amtrak services.

The attack adds to growing concerns about public safety in major urban transit centers. Penn Station sees hundreds of thousands of passengers pass through daily, making it a critical piece of infrastructure for the region. Law enforcement officials have not yet released information about a possible motive for the attack.

The incident unfolded as travelers moved through the station during regular operations. Witnesses described scenes of chaos as emergency responders arrived on scene. The station remained operational following the attack, though some areas were cordoned off as part of the investigation.

New York City officials have increased security measures at transit hubs in recent years following various incidents. This attack represents one of the more significant violent episodes at Penn Station in recent memory, given the number of people injured in a single event. Investigators continue to gather evidence and interview witnesses to piece together the full sequence of events.

cards.headline: Gunmen sought after shooting injures 12 at Toledo festival
cards.teaser: Authorities are searching for suspects after gunfire erupted near a street festival in Toledo, Ohio, injuring 12 people.
cards.body:
A shooting near the Old West End Festival in Toledo, Ohio on Saturday evening left 12 people wounded, with two reported in critical condition. Police believe at least two shooters were involved and say they were likely firing at each other when the gunfire erupted just after 5:30 p.m. near the annual event featuring live music and architectural home tours.

The search for suspects continued into Sunday as festival organizers cancelled the day's planned events. Law enforcement has not announced any arrests in connection with the incident.

cards.headline: Raman moves into second place in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman has overtaken Spencer Pratt for second place in the Los Angeles mayoral primary, positioning herself to face the incumbent in a runoff.
cards.body:
Updated results show Nithya Raman has moved ahead of Spencer Pratt into second place in the Los Angeles mayoral race. The progressive challenger now appears likely to face the current mayor in a runoff election. Pratt, a reality television personality, has fallen to third place as vote counting continues.

The race narrows the field to two main contenders after a crowded primary. Raman's campaign focused on progressive policy positions and local governance issues. The final results will determine whether the mayoral contest moves to a general election runoff between the top two finishers.

cards.headline: Man and two children found dead in Canoga Park shooting
cards.teaser: Three people, including twin 10-year-old boys, were found dead in what police are investigating as an apparent murder-suicide in Canoga Park.
cards.body:
A man and two children were found dead after a shooting in Canoga Park, according to police. Authorities are investigating the incident as an apparent murder-suicide. The two children were identified as twin 10-year-old boys.

Los Angeles Police Department officers responded to the scene where all three victims were discovered. The shooting occurred at a residence in the Canoga Park neighborhood. Investigators are working to determine the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

cards.headline: Trump ends NBC interview after dispute over election claims
cards.teaser: Former President Trump walked out of a Meet the Press interview after clashing with the host over his claims about the 2020 election.
cards.body:
Donald Trump walked out of an NBC Meet the Press interview after a tense exchange with host Kristen Welker. The confrontation occurred during a Friday interview in Wisconsin that aired on Sunday, with Welker repeatedly challenging Trump's claims that the 2020 presidential election and California governor races were rigged.

The abrupt exit came as Trump made unsubstantiated assertions about the election results. The interview also touched on questions regarding compensation for those charged in the January 6 insurrection.

cards.headline: Maine Democrats divided over Senate candidate Platner amid allegations
cards.teaser: Graham Platner's Senate campaign continues despite allegations of misconduct, with Democrats in Maine expressing mixed reactions to his candidacy.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a former Marine and oyster farmer seeking to unseat Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine, is pressing forward with his Senate campaign following allegations of misconduct. He has faced accusations including sending sexually explicit messages to women while married and having a Nazi-themed tattoo.

Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna defended Platner's candidacy on Sunday, acknowledging that "his actions were misogynistic, they were shameful, they were wrong," but stated they did not surprise Maine residents. The incident has created tension within the Democratic Party as members weigh their support for Platner's bid.

cards.headline: Tech stocks decline in Asian markets after Middle East tensions rise
cards.teaser: Stock markets in South Korea and Japan dropped following renewed attacks in the Middle East, ending a recent rally in technology stocks.
cards.body:
Markets in South Korea and Japan experienced declines following a recent rally in technology stocks. The selloff came as renewed military actions in the Middle East prompted investors to reassess their positions.

The market movements reflect investor concerns about how regional conflicts could impact global trade and economic growth. Asian markets typically respond to geopolitical developments that threaten international economic stability.

cards.headline: OPEC Plus increases oil output despite Strait of Hormuz shutdown
cards.teaser: The cartel announced a production increase of 188,000 barrels per day as vast oil supplies remain stranded.
cards.body:
OPEC Plus announced it will boost oil production by 188,000 barrels per day as a ceasefire in Iran remains elusive. The move comes as the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz has stranded vast amounts of the world's oil supply, limiting the practical impact of any production increases.

Analysts described the production boost as largely symbolic given the current state of global oil transportation. The strait closure continues to prevent normal oil shipment routes, creating a disconnect between production capacity and delivery capability that has driven prices higher despite the announced output increase.

cards.headline: Nvidia strikes partnerships with South Korean tech firms for AI infrastructure
cards.teaser: The chip maker announced deals with SK Group and other Korean companies to advance AI development.
cards.body:
Nvidia has secured partnerships with South Korean technology leaders including SK Group to strengthen its presence in the region's AI infrastructure market. The company announced a multiyear technology collaboration with SK Hynix focused on developing memory chips for AI applications, with Nvidia's new Vera chip incorporating SK Hynix memory components.

South Korea's Naver is constructing gigawatt-scale AI facilities powered by Nvidia technology as part of broader regional efforts to expand AI capabilities. These agreements underscore growing demand for advanced AI infrastructure among major South Korean technology companies.

cards.headline: Nvidia tops Wall Street Journal's 2026 list of best companies for the future
cards.teaser: The chip maker secured the top ranking in an annual assessment of companies built for long-term success.
cards.body:
Nvidia claimed the top position on the Wall Street Journal's 2026 ranking of best companies for the future. The list identifies companies well-positioned to thrive amid rapid change, using criteria including innovation capacity, market position, and adaptability.

The Journal published its methodology alongside the results, detailing how it evaluated businesses for sustained success potential. The ranking recognizes Nvidia's continued dominance in the AI chip market and its expanding global partnerships with technology companies.

cards.headline: Spain records highest-ever April visitor numbers as tourists avoid Middle East
cards.teaser: The European country received 9.1 million international visitors in April, a record for the month.
cards.body: Spain welcomed 9.1 million international visitors in April, breaking the record for the highest number of tourists in a single month. The surge reflects a shift in travel patterns, as visitors redirect their vacation plans away from Middle East destinations amid regional conflicts. Spain's Mediterranean appeal has made it an attractive alternative for travelers reassessing where to spend their holidays during this period of geopolitical uncertainty.

cards.headline: Netherlands achieves world-leading youth employment rates
cards.teaser: The country maintains one of the lowest rates globally of young people not in education, employment, or training.
cards.body:
The Netherlands has achieved one of the world's lowest rates of 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment, or training. Dutch policymakers emphasize a 'no dead ends' approach that ensures young people have pathways to continued education or work opportunities.

The success of the Dutch model has drawn international attention as other countries struggle with youth unemployment challenges. The system focuses on providing multiple options for young people to remain engaged in productive activities, whether through traditional education, vocational training, or employment programs.

cards.headline: Apple prepares new AI features for WWDC after previous setbacks
cards.teaser: Apple will present updated AI capabilities at its Worldwide Developers Conference following two years of challenges with its Siri assistant.
cards.body:
Apple is set to unveil new artificial intelligence features at its Worldwide Developers Conference. The announcements follow what Reuters describes as two years of setbacks for the company's AI efforts. The event will showcase updates to iOS 27, macOS 27, and a revised version of Siri powered by Google's Gemini technology.

The keynote will stream live, giving Apple a second opportunity to demonstrate its AI strategy. Industry observers are watching to see how the company addresses previous shortcomings in its voice assistant and other AI-powered services. The conference represents a critical moment for Apple as competitors have advanced their own AI offerings.

cards.headline: Axiom Space and Prada unveil liquid cooling garment for moon missions
cards.teaser: NASA astronauts will wear Prada-engineered undergarments with liquid cooling technology during Artemis IV lunar missions.
cards.body:
Axiom Space and luxury fashion house Prada revealed a liquid cooling garment designed for the AxEMU moonsuit. The undergarment will be worn by NASA astronauts during Artemis IV missions to the lunar surface. The collaboration represents Prada's entry into space industry engineering.

The cooling system addresses temperature regulation challenges astronauts face during moon walks. Prada contributed design and materials expertise to the garment's development. The partnership between a luxury brand and space technology company marks an unusual crossover in aerospace engineering.

cards.headline: Xbox announces Gears of War: E-Day as console exclusive for October release
cards.teaser: Microsoft revealed Gears of War: E-Day will launch exclusively on Xbox Series X/S and PC this October, not appearing on PlayStation 5.
cards.body:
Microsoft revealed Gears of War: E-Day at its Xbox Games Showcase, confirming it will launch as an Xbox console exclusive. The game will not come to PlayStation 5, despite earlier rumors suggesting a PS5 release alongside Xbox and PC versions.

The exclusivity announcement marks a notable shift in Microsoft's approach. The company has previously brought some titles to competing platforms, making this return to platform exclusives a significant strategic move for the Gears of War franchise.

cards.headline: Atlus announces Persona 6 at Xbox Games Showcase
cards.teaser: The sixth mainline Persona game was officially revealed with graveyard visuals and a green color scheme after leaked images circulated online.
cards.body:
Atlus officially confirmed Persona 6 during the 2026 Xbox Games Showcase at Summer Game Fest. The announcement came as a brief teaser, marking the long-awaited return of the mainline Persona series following years of fan anticipation.

The reveal occurred alongside other major Japanese RPG announcements at the event, including the conclusion of the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy at SGF Live.

cards.headline: Valheim sets September 9 release date for version 1.0
cards.teaser: The Viking survival game will exit early access after nearly five years, adding a final biome called the Deep North.
cards.body:
Iron Gate Studio has announced that Valheim will launch version 1.0 on September 9, marking the completion of the Viking survival game's development roadmap after nearly five years in early access.

The final release introduces the Deep North, a new biome featuring treacherously icy terrain populated with ghost vikings, moose, and ancient threats. Valheim will also release on Nintendo Switch 2 with its own dedicated launch date and trailer.

cards.headline: Sega confirms use of generative AI in Crazy Taxi World Tour development
cards.teaser: The rebooted arcade game, set for 2027 release, incorporated AI-generated content during its development process.
cards.body:
Sega confirmed that generative artificial intelligence was used during development of Crazy Taxi World Tour. The game reboots the 1999 arcade classic and is scheduled for release in 2027. Sega issued a statement responding to questions about AI content in the game.

The announcement also revealed that a 1990s punk rock band will reunite to contribute music to the title. Crazy Taxi World Tour will be available on Xbox and other platforms. The use of generative AI in game development has become a topic of discussion across the industry.

hero.headline: Spurs face elimination in Game 3 at Madison Square Garden
hero.teaser: Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs head to Madison Square Garden for Game 3 down 0-2 in the NBA Finals against the Knicks.
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs trail the New York Knicks 2-0 in the NBA Finals heading into Game 3 at Madison Square Garden on Monday night. Victor Wembanyama and his teammates have expressed confidence in their ability to stage a comeback despite the significant deficit.

This matchup marks the first NBA Finals game at Madison Square Garden since June 25, 1999. The Spurs must win to avoid falling into a 3-0 hole in the series, which would put them on the brink of elimination.

The Knicks' dominant start has caught the attention of prominent figures beyond the sports world. President Donald Trump, a longtime Knicks fan, said he plans to attend Game 3 as a guest of team owner James Dolan. Trump watched portions of Game 1, which the Knicks won to take a 1-0 series lead. He praised the team's performance, noting their effective defense against Wembanyama. "I say, how do you guard this guy? He's 7ft 5in and he's got a great shot, right? But they find a way to do it. They're really great," Trump said.

The NBA believes Trump would be the first sitting president to attend an NBA Finals game. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver noted that Trump has been a Knicks fan for decades, attending games and events at Madison Square Garden long before his political career began.

Trump's attendance at Game 3 has prompted significant security preparations. The New York Police Department announced enhanced security measures for the event, including the cancellation of a planned watch party outside Madison Square Garden. These security arrangements are expected to create logistical challenges for fans, including longer transit times to reach the arena.

Silver acknowledged the security requirements but suggested fans understand the added measures. "I think the fans are very understanding of that," Silver said. "I think they recognize that it adds to the bigness of the event."

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has also indicated plans to attend Monday's game, though he suggested he will be seated in a different section of the arena from Trump. The mayor's office said he would purchase his own ticket, which were selling for more than $8,000 on the secondary market as of Thursday.

Despite the political attention surrounding Game 3, the focus remains on the basketball. The Spurs face a critical moment in the Finals, needing to win to keep their championship hopes alive. The team's ability to contend with the Knicks' dominant defense and execution will determine whether they can begin their comeback or face elimination from the championship series.

cards.headline: Nelly Korda wins U.S. Women's Open for second straight major
cards.teaser: Nelly Korda won the U.S.
cards.body:
Nelly Kord won the U.S. Women's Open on Sunday for her first title in the tournament and her second consecutive major championship. She finished one stroke ahead of Charley Hull and Gaby Lopez, securing the $2.5 million first prize. The victory came down to a dramatic final hole, where her 2½-foot par putt curved around the cup before dropping in.

The win marks Kord's fourth major championship overall. She shot a steady two-under 69 in the final round to capture the title during what has been a dominant season in women's golf. Hull, from England, missed out on claiming her first major victory in the close finish.

cards.headline: Denmark match called off after Christian Eriksen collapses on field
cards.teaser: A friendly match between Denmark and Ukraine was canceled after Christian Eriksen collapsed during play.
cards.body:
Denmark's friendly match against Ukraine was abandoned after midfielder Christian Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during the game in Odense on Sunday. Medical personnel immediately attended to the player, and the Danish Football Association confirmed he was conscious after receiving treatment.

This was an end-of-season friendly between the two nations. Eriksen, a former Tottenham and Manchester United player, previously suffered cardiac arrest during a European Championship match in 2021.

cards.headline: Alex Bregman takes blame for Cubs offensive struggles in loss
cards.teaser: Chicago third baseman Alex Bregman blamed himself for the Cubs' offensive problems after going hitless in a loss to the Giants.
cards.body:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman accepted responsibility for his team's offensive struggles after going 0-for-5 in a 2-1 loss to the San Francisco Giants. Bregman made the final out of the game and described his own performance as terrible.

Bregman is in the first year of a five-year, $175 million contract with the Cubs. His struggles at the plate contributed to the team's narrow defeat in the low-scoring contest.

cards.headline: Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett to attend mandatory minicamp
cards.teaser: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett will report for the team's mandatory minicamp after missing all offseason workouts.
cards.body:
Jacoby Brissett will report to Arizona's mandatory minicamp this week, ending his holdout from the Cardinals' offseason program. The quarterback has been absent from voluntary activities while seeking a reworked contract for the upcoming season.

Brissett's attendance at mandatory minicamp marks a shift in his stance, though contract negotiations between the quarterback and the team remain ongoing.

cards.headline: Timberwolves unveil new uniforms, logo and court designs
cards.teaser: The Minnesota Timberwolves revealed new team uniforms, a redesigned logo and updated court layouts.
cards.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves have revealed updated uniforms, a refreshed logo and redesigned courts. The team drew inspiration from its franchise history to create the new look, blending recognizable elements from the past with a modern visual identity.

The redesign gives the organization a fresh appearance while maintaining connections to its heritage through the updated uniforms and court designs.

cards.headline: NYPD cancels Madison Square Garden watch party for Game 3
cards.teaser: Police canceled a planned watch party outside Madison Square Garden due to enhanced security for President Trump's attendance.
cards.body:
The New York Police Department canceled a watch party scheduled outside Madison Square Garden for Game 3 of the NBA Finals between the Knicks and Spurs on Monday night. The cancellation was announced Sunday as part of enhanced security measures for President Donald Trump's attendance at the game.

The decision came after coordination between the Secret Service and NYPD. The Knicks advised fans to arrive at least two hours before tipoff and bring minimal belongings. A previous watch party outside the venue during Game 2 resulted in more than 20 arrests as fans celebrated the team's victory.

hero.headline: Death of a Salesman Sweeps Tony Awards with Six Wins
hero.body:
Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman dominated the 2026 Tony Awards, claiming six wins and becoming the most awarded play revival in the ceremony's history. The stripped-back revival earned best revival of a play, with director Joe Mantello accepting the award and reflecting on how Miller's story "still talks to us through time."

Nathan Lane accepted the award on behalf of the cast, calling it a play that "continues to teach us who we are as humans and Americans." His co-star Laurie Metcalf won her third Tony Award for best featured actress in a play, defeating June Squibb and Aya Cash. Death of a Salesman's six wins surpassed the previous record for most awarded play revival. The production has won major recognition before, claiming best play in 1949 and best revival in 1984, 1999, and 2012.

John Lithgow made history as the oldest man to win a competitive acting Tony at age 80. The veteran actor won best leading actor in a play for his role as Roald Dahl in the antisemitism drama Giant, beating Nathan Lane, Mark Strong, and Daniel Radcliffe. Lithgow also won an Olivier award for the same role during the show's West End run. His victory marked his third Tony and came 53 years after his first win. "It's an extraordinarily important play of this moment," he said on stage.

Lesley Manville won best leading actress in a play for her Broadway debut in the stage adaptation of Oedipus. The actor defeated Rose Byrne and Carrie Coon, calling it "such a big deal" to win on her first Broadway appearance after previously winning an Olivier for the same performance.

Other major winners included Liberation, which won best play after recently earning the Pulitzer Prize for Drama. Playwright Bess Wohl called it "the honour of a lifetime." The victory marks the first time a female playwright has won since 2009, making Wohl only the fourth woman to receive the award.

The musical Schmigadoon! took home best musical along with three additional awards. Producer Lorne Michaels accepted the award, noting that "sometimes singing, dancing, a lot of jokes and a happy ending is really all you need."

Ragtime won four Tonys, including best revival of a musical. Joshua Henry and Caissie Levy won leading actor and actress in a musical, respectively. Henry won his first Tony after four previous nominations. "Every artist in this room, every artist at home, fight, fight, fight to be heard," he said during his acceptance speech.

Pink hosted the ceremony for the first time, opening with a star-packed performance of Lady Marmalade featuring Lea Michele and Megan Thee Stallion. The singer called herself "Broadway's biggest fan" and paid tribute to the theater community's hardest workers.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Tops Weekend Box Office with $55 Million Opening
cards.teaser: The R-rated comedy revival topped the box office with a $55 million opening, defeating Masters of the Universe.
cards.body:
Scary Movie led the weekend box office with a $55 million opening, continuing a streak of low-budget film successes. The film defeated Masters of the Universe to claim the top spot and marked a return of politically incorrect humor to mainstream comedy.

The Wayans stars and director participated in promotional interviews about the film's explosive meta finale. Paramount released the horror satire despite mixed reviews questioning whether the franchise could recapture its earlier success.

cards.headline: The Vampire Lestat Premieres, Shifting Focus from Louis's Narration
cards.teaser: The Interview with the Vampire series entered its Lestat-focused era with a season premiere shifting narrative perspective.
cards.body:
The Vampire Lestat premiered with a narrative shift from Louis's point of view to Lestat's perspective. The series stars discussed the differences between the two characters' narrations and how the change affects the storytelling approach.

The premiere episode opened with a scene that sparked viewer discussion about its significance to the season's arc. The series continues to adapt Anne Rice's vampire chronicles, with the new season drawing from the Lestat-focused novels in the series.

cards.headline: FCC Chairman Criticizes Scott Pelley Over 60 Minutes Firing Comments
cards.teaser: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr called journalist Scott Pelley out of touch for saying his 60 Minutes firing surprised him.
cards.body:
CBS News fired veteran 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley after he clashed with the network's new management. Pelley publicly accused executives of instructing him to inject falsehoods and bias into his reporting and of silencing employees.

The firing sparked criticism from FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who characterized Pelley as out of touch for expressing surprise at his dismissal. Carr cited the incident as evidence of disconnect between legacy journalists and the public, contributing to declining trust in traditional media institutions.

cards.headline: Lawsuit Filed to Block Trump UFC Event on White House Lawn
cards.teaser: Two Virginia residents sued to stop President Trump's plan to host UFC Freedom 250 on the White House South Lawn.
cards.body:
Two Virginia residents filed a federal lawsuit Saturday seeking to stop President Donald Trump's plan to host a UFC fight card on the White House South Lawn. The event, called UFC Freedom 250, is scheduled to coincide with Trump's 80th birthday and is being promoted as part of celebrations for America's 250th anniversary.

The lawsuit was filed against the National Park Service and the Department of the Interior. The planned event would represent an unusual use of White House grounds for a commercial sporting event.

cards.headline: Luke Evans Performs in Minimal Rocky Horror Costume at Tony Awards
cards.teaser: The actor appeared on the Tony Awards stage in a jockstrap, corset, and high heels for The Rocky Horror Show.
cards.body:
Luke Evans performed at the Tony Awards wearing minimal costume pieces including a jockstrap, corset, and high heels as part of The Rocky Horror Show presentation. Evans attended the ceremony with partner Fran Tomas, with the couple wearing coordinating looks on the red carpet.

Evans has been performing in the Broadway revival of The Rocky Horror Show. He recently discussed his preparation routine in an interview, describing his 24-hour schedule around performances of the cult musical.

cards.headline: Angelina Jolie Attends Son Knox's High School Graduation
cards.teaser: The actress attended her son Knox's high school graduation ceremony ahead of his planned Muay Thai fight.
cards.body:
Angelina Jolie was spotted at her son Knox's high school graduation ceremony, beaming with pride at the milestone event. Knox is one of Jolie's twin sons with former partner Brad Pitt.

Following his graduation, Knox is set to compete in a Muay Thai fight, marking an exciting new chapter ahead.

hero.headline: Trump urges Netanyahu not to retaliate against Iran missile attack
hero.teaser: President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu not to retaliate against Iran's missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy, according to.
hero.body:
President Trump called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, urging him to refrain from retaliating against Iran's missile attack and to pursue diplomatic solutions instead. Trump had previously indicated his intention to make this appeal to Netanyahu.

Despite Trump's request, the Israeli Air Force struck Iranian military targets in central and western Iran on Monday morning. The strikes marked Israel's first direct attack on Iran since an April ceasefire and were launched in response to Iran's initial missile barrage. Trump has rejected suggestions that the escalating conflict contradicts his 2024 campaign pledge to avoid new wars.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges UFC fight planned for White House South Lawn
cards.teaser: A legal filing argues the Trump administration's authorization of a June 14 UFC event at the White House was unlawful.
cards.body:
A federal lawsuit aims to stop a UFC fight card scheduled for the White House South Lawn on June 14, which falls on President Trump's 80th birthday. The event is being promoted as part of celebrations marking the nation's 250th anniversary.

The legal challenge questions whether the Trump administration lawfully authorized hosting a commercial mixed martial arts event on White House grounds.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico governor primary
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body: Former Biden administration Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the New Mexico Democratic primary for governor. If elected in November's general election, she would become the first female Native American governor in the United States. Haaland will face the Republican nominee in the race to lead New Mexico.

cards.headline: Bass and Raman advance to Los Angeles mayoral runoff
cards.teaser: Mayor Karen Bass will face Councilmember Nithya Raman in November after primary results narrowed the field.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and Councilmember Nithya Raman are projected to face off in November to lead the country's second largest city, according to Decision Desk HQ. With 87 percent of votes counted, Bass held 34.68 percent and Raman had 27.12 percent.

Raman gained ground on Republican candidate Spencer Pratt in the vote count, moving from third place into second. Bass, the incumbent Democrat, will compete against Raman, also a Democrat, in the general election to determine who leads Los Angeles for the next term.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Republicans Steve Hilton and Chad Bianco and Democrats Xavier Becerra, Katie Porter, and Tom Steyer compete to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in California's governor primary as candidates vie for nominations to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are competing for their party's nomination, while Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra seek the Democratic slot.

The primary will determine which two candidates advance to the general election under California's top-two primary system. Results continue to be tallied as voters choose who will compete to lead the nation's most populous state.

cards.headline: Children's wellbeing declined nationally since before pandemic
cards.teaser: Kids in 29 states are faring worse than before COVID-19, according to a new report on child wellbeing from 2019 to 2024.
cards.body:
Children's wellbeing declined nationally from 2019 to 2024, with kids in 29 states faring worse than before the COVID pandemic, according to a new report. The decline affects multiple measures of child health, safety, and family stability across the country.

Researchers warn that rising costs and safety-net reductions could further strain families. Children's wellbeing affects future workforce participation and economic growth, according to Leslie Boissiere, who noted that kids who are healthy, safe, fed, educated and surrounded by strong family relationships have a better chance to thrive as independent adults.

cards.headline: Trump rejects claim Iran war betrayed campaign promise
cards.teaser: The president dismissed suggestions that the conflict with Iran contradicts his 2024 campaign pledge of no new wars.
cards.body:
President Trump is dismissing claims that military involvement with Iran contradicts his 2024 campaign promise to avoid new wars. The president made ending military conflicts a centerpiece of his campaign messaging.

Tensions with Iran have escalated into active conflict, including missile exchanges between Iran and Israel. Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to hold off on retaliating against Iran's missile attack and pursue diplomatic solutions instead, according to U.S. and Israeli officials.
